long_biography.plain_text:
Lukas van der Valk grew up inside the family enterprise that his father Arie helped turn into a Dutch hospitality institution. Rather than remaining a passive family shareholder, he and his wife Hellen took over the A4 bridge restaurant near Schiphol. They developed it from a 220-room hotel in 1992 into a property with more than 600 rooms under the next generation.

As chairman of the family's Voorschoten branch, Van der Valk oversaw a broad hotel portfolio and encouraged expansion beyond motorway locations. His branch included De Gouden Leeuw in Voorschoten, Hotel Schiphol and Amsterdam Zuidas, a later architectural landmark. Colleagues remembered an ambitious perfectionist whose operating ideas helped modernise the group's hospitality offering before his death in 2023.
